"""The interface for all transforms.

This module defines the base classes and interfaces for all transforms.
"""

import os
import time
from abc import ABC
from contextlib import contextmanager, nullcontext
from dataclasses import dataclass
from enum import Enum
from functools import total_ordering, wraps
from typing import Any, Callable, Dict, Mapping, Optional, Tuple, Type, Union, final

import torch
import torch.nn as nn
from pydantic import BaseModel, Field
from torch.fx import GraphModule, Node

from ..models.factory import ModelFactory
from ..shim.interface import CachedSequenceInterface
from ..utils._graph import (
    add_graph_input,
    canonicalize_graph,
    lift_to_meta,
    named_graphmodules,
    placeholders_on_meta,
    run_shape_prop,
)
from ..utils.cuda_mem_tracker import get_mem_info
from ..utils.dist_config import DistConfig  # kept in utils to avoid circular imports
from ..utils.graph_writer import graph_writer
from ..utils.logger import ad_logger
from .graph_module_visualizer import to_dot

# ANSI color codes for log formatting (set to False to disable colors)
# NOTE: colors disabled by default to make logging in CI/CD pipelines easier to read
_ENABLE_LOG_COLORS = False


class _Colors:
    RESET = "\033[0m" if _ENABLE_LOG_COLORS else ""
    BOLD = "\033[1m" if _ENABLE_LOG_COLORS else ""
    DIM = "\033[2m" if _ENABLE_LOG_COLORS else ""
    CYAN = "\033[36m" if _ENABLE_LOG_COLORS else ""
    MAGENTA = "\033[35m" if _ENABLE_LOG_COLORS else ""
    GREEN = "\033[32m" if _ENABLE_LOG_COLORS else ""
    YELLOW = "\033[33m" if _ENABLE_LOG_COLORS else ""
    ORANGE = "\033[38;5;208m" if _ENABLE_LOG_COLORS else ""


@dataclass
class MemStats:
    """Memory statistics snapshot for tracking CUDA memory usage."""

    tot: float
    free: float
    resv: float
    alloc: float
    frag: float

    def diff(self, other: "MemStats") -> "MemStats":
        """Calculate the difference (self - other)."""
        return MemStats(
            tot=self.tot - other.tot,
            free=self.free - other.free,
            resv=self.resv - other.resv,
            alloc=self.alloc - other.alloc,
            frag=self.frag - other.frag,
        )

    def to_dict(self) -> Dict[str, float]:
        """Convert to dictionary for serialization."""
        return {
            "tot": self.tot,
            "free": self.free,
            "resv": self.resv,
            "alloc": self.alloc,
            "frag": self.frag,
        }

    @classmethod
    def from_dict(cls, d: Dict[str, float]) -> "MemStats":
        """Create from dictionary."""
        return cls(tot=d["tot"], free=d["free"], resv=d["resv"], alloc=d["alloc"], frag=d["frag"])


class TransformError(Exception):
    """An exception raised when a transform fails."""

    pass


@total_ordering
class Stages(Enum):
    """Enumerated (ordered!) stages of the transformation pipeline.

    This is used to classify and pre-order transforms.
    """

    FACTORY = "factory"  # factory stage for building the model
    EXPORT = "export"  # export stage for exporting the model to a graph module
    POST_EXPORT = "post_export"  # low-level cleanups of the exported graph
    PATTERN_MATCHER = "pattern_matcher"  # high-level pattern matching to standardize graph
    SHARDING = "sharding"  # auto-sharding of the graph
    WEIGHT_LOAD = "weight_load"  # loading of the model weights
    POST_LOAD_FUSION = "post_load_fusion"  # post-loading fusion and perf optimizations of the graph
    CACHE_INIT = "cache_init"  # initialization of cached attention + (KV) cache initialization
    VISUALIZE = "visualize"  # visualization of the graph
    COMPILE = "compile"  # graph compilation stage using low-level compilers like torch.compile

    def __lt__(self, other):
        """Enable sorting by definition order."""
        if self.__class__ is other.__class__:
            return list(self.__class__).index(self) < list(other.__class__).index(other)
        return NotImplemented


class SharedConfig(BaseModel):
    """Global config shared between multiple transforms in the inference optimizer."""

    model_config = {
        # to provide an easy way to do config validation of child config classes with more fields
        "extra": "allow",
        "arbitrary_types_allowed": True,
    }
    local_rank: int = Field(default=0)
    world_size: int = Field(default=1)
    dist_config: Optional[DistConfig] = Field(default=None)


class TransformConfig(BaseModel):
    """A simple configuration class that can be extended by a transform for configurability."""

    model_config = {
        # to provide an easy way to do config validation of child config classes with more fields
        "extra": "allow",
    }

    ### MANDATORY CONFIG ###########################################################################
    stage: Stages = Field(
        description="The stage of the transformation pipeline where this transform should run.",
    )

    ### OPTIONAL CONFIG ###########################################################################
    run_per_gm: bool = Field(
        description="Whether to run the transform per graph (sub)module or on whole module.",
        default=True,
    )
    enabled: bool = Field(
        default=True,
        description="Whether to enable this transform.",
    )
    skip_on_error: bool = Field(
        default=False,
        description="Whether to skip the transform if an error occurs.",
    )

    run_graph_cleanup: bool = Field(
        default=True,
        description="Whether to run graph cleanup/canonicalization after this transform.",
    )
    run_shape_prop: bool = Field(
        default=False,
        description="Whether to run shape propagation after this transform.",
    )

    requires_clean_graph: bool = Field(
        default=True,
        description="Whether this transform requires the graph to be clean before it is applied.",
    )
    requires_shape_prop: bool = Field(
        default=False,
        description="Whether this transform requires shape propagation before it is applied.",
    )
    debug_visualize_dir: Optional[str] = Field(
        default=None,
        description="Debug visualization directory. None to disable visualization, "
        "or a path string to specify the output directory.",
    )

    expect_mem_change: bool = Field(
        default=False,
        description="Whether this transform is expected to cause changes in CUDA memory stats.",
    )


AutodeployMeta = Dict[str, Any]
_UntypedInferenceOptimizerConfig = Dict[str, Any]
StrictInferenceOptimizerConfig = Dict[str, TransformConfig]
InferenceOptimizerConfig = Mapping[str, Union[TransformConfig, _UntypedInferenceOptimizerConfig]]


class TransformInfo(BaseModel):
    """Information about the result of a transform."""

    model_config = {
        "frozen": True,  # Make the model immutable after creation
    }

    skipped: bool = Field(
        default=True,
        description="Whether the transform was skipped.",
    )
    num_matches: int = Field(
        default=0,
        description="Number of matches found.",
    )
    is_clean: bool = Field(
        default=False,
        description="Whether the graph is clean after the transform. This can be set by the "
        "transform to indicate that the transform does not change the graph and it preserves the "
        "is_clean flag of the last transform.",
    )
    has_valid_shapes: bool = Field(
        default=False,
        description="Whether meta tensor shapes are valid after the transform. This can be set by "
        "the transform to indicate that the transform does not affect the shapes in the meta "
        "information of the graph. In other words, the transform does not change the shapes of the "
        "tensors in the graph and it preserves the has_valid_shapes flag of the last transform.",
    )

    @classmethod
    def from_last_info(cls, info: "TransformInfo") -> "TransformInfo":
        """Create a new TransformInfo from the last transform info."""
        return cls(
            is_clean=info.is_clean,
            has_valid_shapes=info.has_valid_shapes,
        )

    def __or__(self, other: "TransformInfo") -> "TransformInfo":
        """Merge two TransformInfo objects."""
        return TransformInfo(
            skipped=self.skipped and other.skipped,  # we only count skipped if both were skipped
            num_matches=self.num_matches + other.num_matches,
            is_clean=self.is_clean or other.is_clean,
            has_valid_shapes=self.has_valid_shapes or other.has_valid_shapes,
        )

    def __and__(self, other: "TransformInfo") -> "TransformInfo":
        """Merge two TransformInfo objects."""
        return TransformInfo(
            skipped=self.skipped and other.skipped,  # we only count skipped if both were skipped
            num_matches=self.num_matches + other.num_matches,
            is_clean=self.is_clean and other.is_clean,
            has_valid_shapes=self.has_valid_shapes and other.has_valid_shapes,
        )

    # implement + addition operator for TransformInfo
    def __add__(self, other: "TransformInfo") -> "TransformInfo":
        return self.__and__(other)


TransformHistory = Dict[str, TransformInfo]


def with_transform_logging(call_fn: Callable) -> Callable:
    """Decorator to prepend transform-specific prefix to all ad_logger logs during __call__.

    Temporarily patches `ad_logger.log` so that any logs emitted within the call automatically
    include the `[stage=..., transform=...]` prefix that `_log_info` would otherwise add manually.
    The original logger behavior is restored after the call, even if an exception occurs.
    """

    @wraps(call_fn)
    def _wrapper(
        self,
        gm: nn.Module,
        cm: CachedSequenceInterface,
        factory: ModelFactory,
        shared_config: SharedConfig,
        idx: int,
    ) -> nn.Module:
        prefix = f"[stage={self.config.stage.value}, transform={self.get_transform_key()}]"
        original_log = ad_logger.log

        def _patched_log(severity, *msg):
            if msg and isinstance(msg[0], str) and msg[0].startswith(prefix):
                return original_log(severity, *msg)
            return original_log(severity, prefix, *msg)

        ad_logger.log = _patched_log  # type: ignore[assignment]
        try:
            return call_fn(self, gm, cm, factory, shared_config, idx)
        finally:
            ad_logger.log = original_log  # type: ignore[assignment]

    return _wrapper


class BaseTransform(ABC):
    """A base class for all transforms."""

    config: TransformConfig  # overwrite type hint if other config cls is used in subclass!
    _autodeploy_meta_key: str = "_autodeploy"
    _history_key: str = "transform_history"
    _mem_history_key: str = "mem_history"
    _transform_key: str  # Set by TransformRegistry.register() decorator

    @classmethod
    def get_transform_key(cls) -> str:
        """Get the short name of the transform.

        This is used to identify the transform in the transformation pipeline.
        """
        if hasattr(cls, "_transform_key"):
            return cls._transform_key
        raise NotImplementedError(
            f"Transform class {cls.__name__} must be registered with TransformRegistry.register() "
            "or manually implement get_transform_key()"
        )

    @classmethod
    def get_config_class(cls) -> Type[TransformConfig]:
        """Get the configuration class for the transform.

        This is used to validate the configuration of the transform.
        """
        return TransformConfig

    @final
    def __init__(self, config: TransformConfig):
        """Initialize the transform.

        Args:
            config: The configuration for the transform, either as base config object or the actual
                config object.

        To customize the initialization, override the `_post_init` method.
        """
        if not isinstance(config, self.get_config_class()):
            config = self.get_config_class()(**config.model_dump())
        self.config = config
        self._post_init()

    def _post_init(self):
        """Post-initialization hook that can be overridden by subclasses."""
        pass

    @final
    @classmethod
    def from_kwargs(cls, **kwargs) -> "BaseTransform":
        """Create a transform from kwargs.

        Args:
            **kwargs: The configuration for the transform.

        Returns:
            The transform instance.
        """
        config = cls.get_config_class()(**kwargs)
        return cls(config=config)

    @with_transform_logging
    @final
    def __call__(
        self,
        mod: nn.Module,
        cm: CachedSequenceInterface,
        factory: ModelFactory,
        shared_config: SharedConfig,
        idx: int,
    ) -> nn.Module:
        """Apply the transform to the graph.

        Args:
            mod: The model to apply the transform to.
            cm: The cached sequence interface defining the sequence interface.
            factory: The model factory used to build the model.
            shared_config: Global info shared between multiple transforms.
            idx: The index of the transform in the pipeline.

        Returns:
            nn.Module: The transformed model.

        NOTE: The transform can/should modify the graph module in place if possible. Returning the
        graph is mostly to standardize the interface for transforms that cannot modify the graph
        in place (e.g. the factory or export transform).

        This method is the main entry point for any transforms and is called by the
        InferenceOptimizer pipeline.
        """

        # get the transform key
        t_name = self.get_transform_key()

        # retrieve autodeploy metadata from the graphmodule
        autodeploy_meta = self._get_autodeploy_meta(mod)

        # retrieve transform history and last transform info
        history: TransformHistory = autodeploy_meta.get(self._history_key, {})
        h_keys = list(history.keys())  # preserves order of insertion/transform execution
        info_last = history[h_keys[-1]] if h_keys else TransformInfo(skipped=False, num_matches=0)

        # initialize new info object
        info = TransformInfo.from_last_info(info_last)

        # show debug info for debug config
        ad_logger.debug(f"{t_name} config: {self.config}")

        # capture memory stats at the start
        mem_pre = self._get_mem_stats(empty_cache=True)

        # store some timing information
        elapsed_time_total = -time.time()
        elapsed_time_pre_cleanup = 0.0
        elapsed_time_apply = 0.0
        elapsed_time_post_cleanup = 0.0

        # run or skip the transform
        if self.config.enabled:
            # run graph pre-cleanup and update info object
            elapsed_time_pre_cleanup = -time.time()
            info = info | self._run_cleanup(
                mod,
                self.config.requires_clean_graph,
                self.config.requires_shape_prop,
                info.is_clean,
                info.has_valid_shapes,
                phase="pre",
            )
            elapsed_time_pre_cleanup += time.time()

            # run the transform in a error-handling wrapper if desired
            elapsed_time_apply = -time.time()
            with self._apply_logging_context():
                self._log_info("applying transform...")
                if self.config.skip_on_error:
                    try:
                        mod, info_apply = self._apply_per_gm_or_whole_model(
                            mod, cm, factory, shared_config
                        )
                    except Exception as e:
                        error_msg = f"Transform {t_name} failed"
                        ad_logger.warning(f"{error_msg}: {e}")
                        info_apply = TransformInfo(skipped=True, num_matches=0)
                else:
                    # handle this here normally to improve debugging and error message
                    mod, info_apply = self._apply_per_gm_or_whole_model(
                        mod, cm, factory, shared_config
                    )
            elapsed_time_apply += time.time()

            # we cannot say it's clean if the previous wasn't clean even if this one is
            # create new info object with updated cleanup status
            info = info & info_apply

            # run graph post-cleanup
            elapsed_time_post_cleanup = -time.time()
            info = info | self._run_cleanup(
                mod,
                self.config.run_graph_cleanup,
                self.config.run_shape_prop,
                info.is_clean,
                info.has_valid_shapes,
                phase="post",
            )
            elapsed_time_post_cleanup += time.time()

        elapsed_time_total += time.time()

        # capture memory stats at the end and log summary (only log if enabled)
        mem_post = self._get_mem_stats(empty_cache=True)
        if self.config.enabled:
            self._log_mem_summary(mem_pre, mem_post, self.config.expect_mem_change)

        # log the result of the transform
        self._log_transform_summary(
            enabled=self.config.enabled,
            skipped=info.skipped,
            num_matches=info.num_matches,
            elapsed_total=elapsed_time_total,
            elapsed_pre=elapsed_time_pre_cleanup,
            elapsed_apply=elapsed_time_apply,
            elapsed_post=elapsed_time_post_cleanup,
        )
        ad_logger.debug(f"Model after {t_name}: {mod}")

        # update + store new meta data (transform history and memory history)
        history[t_name] = info
        autodeploy_meta[self._history_key] = history

        # store memory history
        mem_history: Dict[str, Dict[str, Dict[str, float]]] = autodeploy_meta.get(
            self._mem_history_key, {}
        )
        mem_history[t_name] = {"pre": mem_pre.to_dict(), "post": mem_post.to_dict()}
        autodeploy_meta[self._mem_history_key] = mem_history

        self._set_autodeploy_meta(mod, autodeploy_meta)
        self._visualize_graph(mod, idx)

        # Dump graph after transform for debugging (controlled by AD_DUMP_GRAPHS_DIR env var)
        graph_writer.dump_graph(mod, t_name, self.config.stage.value)

        # return the graph module
        return mod

    @final
    def _visualize_graph(self, mod: nn.Module, idx: int) -> None:
        """Visualize the graph if debug visualization is enabled.
        Args:
            mod: The graph module to visualize.
            idx: The index of the transform in the pipeline.
        Note:
            we may want to consider doing this for each subgraph.
            See https://github.com/NVIDIA/TensorRT-LLM/issues/10203
        """
        if not isinstance(mod, torch.fx.GraphModule):
            return
        visualize_dir = self.config.debug_visualize_dir
        if not visualize_dir:
            return
        if not os.path.exists(visualize_dir):
            os.makedirs(visualize_dir)
        name_stem = f"gm_{idx + 1:02d}_{self.get_transform_key()}"
        visualize_path = os.path.join(visualize_dir, f"{name_stem}")
        to_dot(mod, name=name_stem, save_path=visualize_path, format="svg")
        ad_logger.debug(f"[{idx + 1:02d}] Visualized {name_stem} to {visualize_path}")

    @final
    def _apply_per_gm_or_whole_model(
        self,
        mod: nn.Module,
        cm: CachedSequenceInterface,
        factory: ModelFactory,
        shared_config: SharedConfig,
    ) -> Tuple[nn.Module, TransformInfo]:
        if not self.config.run_per_gm:
            return self._apply_to_full_model(mod, cm, factory, shared_config)

        # just run it on first graph module we are encountering for now...
        info = None
        for k, graph_sub in named_graphmodules(mod):
            graph_sub, info_apply = self._apply(graph_sub, cm, factory, shared_config)
            if k == "":
                mod = graph_sub
            else:
                mod.set_submodule(k, graph_sub)
            info = info & info_apply if info is not None else info_apply
        return mod, info

    @final
    def _log_warning(self, *args: any):
        """Log a warning message with the transform key."""
        ad_logger.warning(*args)

    @final
    def _log_info(self, *args: any):
        """Log a message with the transform key."""
        ad_logger.info(*args)

    @final
    def _log_debug(self, *args: any):
        """Log a message with the transform key."""
        ad_logger.debug(*args)

    @contextmanager
    def _apply_logging_context(self):
        """Context manager to add [APPLY] prefix to logs during transform execution."""
        original_log = ad_logger.log
        apply_label = "[APPLY]"

        def _patched_log(severity, *msg):
            # Prepend [APPLY] after any existing prefix
            if msg:
                first = msg[0] if isinstance(msg[0], str) else str(msg[0])
                return original_log(severity, f"{apply_label} {first}", *msg[1:])
            return original_log(severity, apply_label)

        ad_logger.log = _patched_log  # type: ignore[assignment]
        try:
            yield
        finally:
            ad_logger.log = original_log  # type: ignore[assignment]

    @final
    def _log_cleanup_status(self, phase: str, action: str, reason: str = "") -> None:
        """Log cleanup status with colored formatting.

        Args:
            phase: "pre" or "post"
            action: "ran" or "skipped"
            reason: Description of what ran or why skipped
        """
        label = f"{_Colors.CYAN}[{phase.upper()}-CLEANUP]{_Colors.RESET}"
        if action == "skipped":
            self._log_info(f"{label} {_Colors.DIM}skipped ({reason}){_Colors.RESET}")
        else:
            self._log_info(f"{label} {reason}")

    @final
    def _log_transform_summary(
        self,
        enabled: bool,
        skipped: bool,
        num_matches: int,
        elapsed_total: float,
        elapsed_pre: float,
        elapsed_apply: float,
        elapsed_post: float,
    ) -> None:
        """Log transform summary with colored formatting.

        Args:
            enabled: Whether the transform was enabled.
            skipped: Whether the transform was skipped.
            num_matches: Number of matches found.
            elapsed_total: Total elapsed time in seconds.
            elapsed_pre: Pre-cleanup elapsed time in seconds.
            elapsed_apply: Apply elapsed time in seconds.
            elapsed_post: Post-cleanup elapsed time in seconds.
        """
        label = f"{_Colors.GREEN}[SUMMARY]{_Colors.RESET}"
        timing_str = (
            f"{elapsed_total:.3f}s "
            f"(pre={elapsed_pre:.3f}s, apply={elapsed_apply:.3f}s, post={elapsed_post:.3f}s)"
        )

        if not enabled:
            self._log_info(f"{label} {_Colors.DIM}disabled{_Colors.RESET}")
        elif skipped:
            self._log_info(f"{label} {_Colors.DIM}skipped{_Colors.RESET} | time: {timing_str}")
        else:
            self._log_info(f"{label} matches={num_matches} | time: {timing_str}")

    @final
    def _get_mem_stats(self, empty_cache: bool = True) -> MemStats:
        """Get current CUDA memory statistics.

        Args:
            empty_cache: Whether to empty the memory cache before getting the memory stats.

        Returns:
            MemStats object with current memory values in GB.
        """
        tot, free, resv, alloc, frag = get_mem_info(empty_cache=empty_cache, unit="GB")
        return MemStats(tot=tot, free=free, resv=resv, alloc=alloc, frag=frag)

    @final
    def _log_mem_summary(self, pre: MemStats, post: MemStats, expect_mem_change: bool) -> None:
        """Log memory summary with diff between pre and post stats.

        Logs one of three cases:
        1. Expected mem change: info log, magenta color
        2. Unexpected mem change: warning log, yellow color
        3. No mem change: debug log, no colors

        Args:
            pre: Memory stats captured before the transform.
            post: Memory stats captured after the transform.
            expect_mem_change: Whether this transform is expected to cause memory changes.
        """
        diff = post.diff(pre)

        # Threshold for detecting significant memory changes (in GB)
        mem_change_threshold = 0.005

        # Check if there was a significant memory change
        has_mem_change = (
            abs(diff.resv) >= mem_change_threshold
            or abs(diff.alloc) >= mem_change_threshold
            or abs(diff.frag) >= mem_change_threshold
            or abs(diff.free) >= mem_change_threshold
        )

        def _fmt_val_with_delta(val: float, delta: float, color: str) -> str:
            """Format value with optional delta in the specified color."""
            val_str = f"{val:6.2f}GB"
            if abs(delta) < mem_change_threshold:
                return val_str
            sign = "+" if delta > 0 else ""
            if color:
                return f"{val_str} {_Colors.BOLD}{color}({sign}{delta:.2f}GB){_Colors.RESET}"
            return f"{val_str} ({sign}{delta:.2f}GB)"

        def _fmt_parts(color: str) -> str:
            """Format all memory parts with the specified color for deltas."""
            parts = [
                f"free: {_fmt_val_with_delta(post.free, diff.free, color)}",
                f"resv: {_fmt_val_with_delta(post.resv, diff.resv, color)}",
                f"alloc: {_fmt_val_with_delta(post.alloc, diff.alloc, color)}",
                f"frag: {_fmt_val_with_delta(post.frag, diff.frag, color)}",
            ]
            return " | ".join(parts)

        if has_mem_change and expect_mem_change:
            # Case 1: Expected mem change - info log, magenta
            label = f"{_Colors.MAGENTA}[CUDA MEM DIFF (EXPECTED)]{_Colors.RESET}"
            self._log_info(f"{label} {_fmt_parts(_Colors.MAGENTA)}")
        elif has_mem_change and not expect_mem_change:
            # Case 2: Unexpected mem change - warning log, yellow
            label = f"{_Colors.YELLOW}[CUDA MEM DIFF (UNEXPECTED)]{_Colors.RESET}"
            self._log_warning(f"{label} {_fmt_parts(_Colors.YELLOW)}")
        else:
            # Case 3: No mem change - debug log, no colors
            self._log_debug(f"[CUDA MEM] {_fmt_parts('')}")

    @final
    def _get_autodeploy_meta(self, mod: nn.Module) -> AutodeployMeta:
        """Get the autodeploy metadata from the graphmodule."""
        if not hasattr(mod, "meta"):
            mod.meta = {}
        return mod.meta.get(self._autodeploy_meta_key, {})

    @final
    def _set_autodeploy_meta(self, mod: nn.Module, autodeploy_meta: AutodeployMeta) -> None:
        """Set the autodeploy metadata in the graphmodule."""
        if not hasattr(mod, "meta"):
            mod.meta = {}
        mod.meta[self._autodeploy_meta_key] = autodeploy_meta

    @final
    def _run_cleanup(
        self,
        mod: nn.Module,
        clean_graph: bool,
        clean_shape: bool,
        is_clean: bool,
        has_valid_shapes: bool,
        phase: str,
    ) -> TransformInfo:
        """Run graph cleanup before or after the transform.

        Args:
            mod: The model to run cleanup on.
            clean_graph: Whether we want a clean graph after the transform.
            clean_shape: Whether we want clean shapes after the transform.
            is_clean: The current cleanup status.
            has_valid_shapes: The current shape propagation status.
            phase: The phase of cleanup ("pre" or "post").

        Returns:
            An info object indicating the cleanup status after this function is called.
        """
        # check if run cleanup depending on the config and info
        if clean_shape and not (is_clean and has_valid_shapes):
            self._log_cleanup_status(phase, "ran", "graph canonicalization + shape_prop")
            canonicalize_graph(mod)
            with lift_to_meta(mod) if placeholders_on_meta(mod) else nullcontext():
                run_shape_prop(mod)
            is_clean = True
            has_valid_shapes = True
        elif clean_graph and not is_clean:
            self._log_cleanup_status(phase, "ran", "graph canonicalization")
            canonicalize_graph(mod)
            is_clean = True
            has_valid_shapes = False
        elif not clean_graph and not clean_shape:
            self._log_cleanup_status(phase, "skipped", "disabled")
        else:
            self._log_cleanup_status(phase, "skipped", "graph already clean")

        return TransformInfo(is_clean=is_clean, has_valid_shapes=has_valid_shapes)

    def _apply(
        self,
        gm: GraphModule,
        cm: CachedSequenceInterface,
        factory: ModelFactory,
        shared_config: SharedConfig,
    ) -> Tuple[GraphModule, TransformInfo]:
        """Apply the transform to the graph.

        This is the core method that should be implemented by subclasses.
        """
        raise NotImplementedError(
            f"Transform {self.get_transform_key()} only supports `run_per_gm=False`."
        )

    def _apply_to_full_model(
        self,
        model: nn.Module,
        cm: CachedSequenceInterface,
        factory: ModelFactory,
        shared_config: SharedConfig,
    ) -> Tuple[nn.Module, TransformInfo]:
        """Apply the transform to the full model."""
        raise NotImplementedError(
            f"Transform {self.get_transform_key()} only supports `run_per_gm=True`."
        )

    def _add_or_retrieve_input(
        self, gm: GraphModule, cm: CachedSequenceInterface, name: str, init_val: bool = False
    ) -> Node:
        """Add or retrieve an input node from the graph."""
        input_nodes = gm.graph.find_nodes(op="placeholder", target=name)
        if len(input_nodes) == 0:
            cm.info.activate_arg(name)
            if init_val:
                # Pass the runtime tensor so add_graph_input populates the
                # placeholder's meta["val"] with a proper FakeTensor (shape +
                # dtype propagated via fake_mode.from_tensor). Leaving meta empty
                # (the default _NO_VAL path) causes downstream transforms that
                # look up node.meta["val"] (FX export, fuse_fp8_linear's pattern
                # matcher) to silently misbehave -- e.g. an adjacent
                # fc2_latent_proj ends up with None in its input slot and the FP8
                # fake impl crashes on `input.dtype`.
                return add_graph_input(gm, name, val=cm.info.get_arg(name))
            else:
                return add_graph_input(gm, name)
        elif len(input_nodes) == 1:
            return input_nodes[0]
        else:
            raise ValueError(f"Expected exactly one input node for {name=}, got {input_nodes=}")


class TransformRegistry:
    """A registry for all transforms."""

    _registry: Dict[str, Type[BaseTransform]] = {}

    @classmethod
    def register(cls, name: str) -> Callable[[Type[BaseTransform]], Type[BaseTransform]]:
        def inner(fn: Type[BaseTransform]) -> Type[BaseTransform]:
            cls._registry[name] = fn
            # Auto-store the transform key as a class attribute
            fn._transform_key = name
            return fn

        return inner

    @classmethod
    def get(cls, name: str) -> Type[BaseTransform]:
        """Get the transform class by name."""
        return cls._registry[name]

    @classmethod
    def get_config_class(cls, name: str) -> Type[TransformConfig]:
        """Get the configuration class for a transform by name."""
        return cls.get(name).get_config_class()

    @classmethod
    def has(cls, name: str) -> bool:
        """Check if a transform is registered."""
        return name in cls._registry

"""High-level entrypoint to transform a model into an efficient inference model."""

import gc
import time
from typing import Optional, Tuple

import torch
import torch.distributed as dist
import torch.nn as nn

from ..distributed import common as dist_ad
from ..models.factory import ModelFactory
from ..shim.interface import CachedSequenceInterface
from ..utils.logger import ad_logger
from .interface import (
    BaseTransform,
    DistConfig,
    InferenceOptimizerConfig,
    SharedConfig,
    Stages,
    StrictInferenceOptimizerConfig,
    TransformConfig,
    TransformRegistry,
)


class InferenceOptimizer:
    def __init__(
        self,
        factory: ModelFactory,
        config: InferenceOptimizerConfig,
        dist_config: Optional[DistConfig] = None,
    ):
        self.factory = factory
        self.config = self._clean_config(config)
        self._cache_key_config = self._copy_config(self.config)
        if not dist.is_initialized():
            local_rank, world_size = 0, 1
        else:
            local_rank, world_size = dist_ad.get_rank_world_size()

        self.shared_config = SharedConfig(
            local_rank=local_rank,
            world_size=world_size,
            dist_config=dist_config,
        )

    def _clean_config(self, config: InferenceOptimizerConfig) -> StrictInferenceOptimizerConfig:
        """Get a typed checked ("strict") config with sorted keys according to stages."""
        # convert to nested kwargs, no TransformConfig objects allowed
        nested_kwargs = {
            k: v.model_dump() if isinstance(v, TransformConfig) else v for k, v in config.items()
        }
        # sort by stage
        keys_sorted = sorted(nested_kwargs.keys(), key=lambda k: Stages(nested_kwargs[k]["stage"]))
        # create strict config with correct config classes and correct order
        strict_config: StrictInferenceOptimizerConfig = {
            k: TransformRegistry.get_config_class(k)(**nested_kwargs[k]) for k in keys_sorted
        }
        # return strict config
        return strict_config

    def _copy_config(
        self, config: StrictInferenceOptimizerConfig
    ) -> StrictInferenceOptimizerConfig:
        """Return a deep copy used for stable cache keys across mutating transforms."""
        return {k: v.model_copy(deep=True) for k, v in config.items()}

    def __call__(self, cm: CachedSequenceInterface, mod: Optional[nn.Module] = None) -> nn.Module:
        """Transform a model into an optimized inference model.

        Args:
            cm: The cached sequence interface defining the sequence interface.
            mod: The model to transform.

        Returns:
            A nn.Module representing the optimized inference model.
        """
        ############################################################################################
        # RUN THROUGH CONFIGURED TRANSFORMATIONS
        ############################################################################################

        can_restore_from_prefix = mod is None

        # start with an empty model if not provided
        if mod is None:
            mod = nn.Module()

        start_time = time.time()
        start_idx = 0
        if can_restore_from_prefix:
            restored_mod, start_idx = self._maybe_restore_from_cache(cm)
            if restored_mod is not None:
                mod = restored_mod

        # iterate over all transforms sorted by stage in the config
        for idx, (t_name, t_config) in enumerate(list(self.config.items())[start_idx:], start_idx):
            # instantiate transform
            transform = self._create_transform(t_name, t_config)
            # run transform
            mod = transform(mod, cm, self.factory, self.shared_config, idx)
        total_time = time.time() - start_time
        ad_logger.info(f"Total time for all transforms: {total_time:.2f}s")

        ############################################################################################
        # RETURN OPTIMIZED MODEL
        ############################################################################################
        torch.cuda.empty_cache()
        gc.collect()
        return mod

    def _maybe_restore_from_cache(
        self, cm: CachedSequenceInterface
    ) -> Tuple[Optional[nn.Module], int]:
        """Ask cache transforms for a restore before running their prefix."""
        for idx, (t_name, t_config) in reversed(list(enumerate(self._cache_key_config.items()))):
            transform_cls = TransformRegistry.get(t_name)
            if not callable(getattr(transform_cls, "maybe_restore", None)):
                continue
            transform = self._create_transform(t_name, t_config)
            restored_mod = transform.maybe_restore(cm, self.factory, self.shared_config, idx)
            if restored_mod is not None:
                return restored_mod, idx + 1
        return None, 0

    def _create_transform(self, t_name: str, t_config: TransformConfig) -> BaseTransform:
        transform = TransformRegistry.get(t_name)(t_config)
        if t_name == "pipeline_cache":
            transform.set_cache_key_config(self._cache_key_config)
        return transform

"""A simple wrapper transform to build a model via the model factory."""

from typing import Tuple, Type

import torch.nn as nn
from pydantic import Field

from ...models import ModelFactory, hf
from ...shim.interface import CachedSequenceInterface
from ..interface import (
    BaseTransform,
    SharedConfig,
    TransformConfig,
    TransformInfo,
    TransformRegistry,
)


class BuildModelConfig(TransformConfig):
    """Configuration for the build model transform."""

    device: str = Field(default="meta", description="The device to build the model on.")


@TransformRegistry.register("build_model")
class BuildModel(BaseTransform):
    """A simple wrapper transform to build a model via the model factory build_model method.

    This transform will build the model via the ``build_model`` method of the model factory on the
    meta device (or the set device) and not load the weights.
    """

    config: BuildModelConfig

    @classmethod
    def get_config_class(cls) -> Type[TransformConfig]:
        return BuildModelConfig

    def _apply_to_full_model(
        self,
        mod: nn.Module,
        cm: CachedSequenceInterface,
        factory: ModelFactory,
        shared_config: SharedConfig,
    ) -> Tuple[nn.Module, TransformInfo]:
        # build the model
        model = factory.build_model(self.config.device)

        # update the kv cache config
        cm.update_kv_cache_config(**factory.get_cache_config_updates())

        # by convention, we say the model is always clean
        info = TransformInfo(skipped=False, num_matches=1, is_clean=True, has_valid_shapes=True)

        return model, info


@TransformRegistry.register("build_and_load_factory_model")
class BuildAndLoadFactoryModel(BuildModel):
    """A simple wrapper transform to build AND load a model via the factory's build_and_load API.

    Under the hood, the factory can use a different way to build and load the model at the same time
    rather than just building the model. For example, the HF factory uses the `.from_pretrained`
    API to directly build and load the model at the same time.

    We also assume that the `build_and_load_model` method will auto-shard the model appropriately.
    """

    config: BuildModelConfig

    def _apply_to_full_model(
        self,
        mod: nn.Module,
        cm: CachedSequenceInterface,
        factory: ModelFactory,
        shared_config: SharedConfig,
    ) -> Tuple[nn.Module, TransformInfo]:
        # load model with auto sharding
        assert isinstance(factory, hf.AutoModelFactory), "Only HF models are supported."

        # build and load the model
        model = factory.build_and_load_model(cm.device)

        # we set the standard example sequence WITHOUT extra_args to set them to None so that
        # only the text portion of the model gets called.
        cm.info.set_example_sequence()

        # by convention, we say this fake graph module is always clean
        info = TransformInfo(skipped=False, num_matches=1, is_clean=True, has_valid_shapes=True)

        return model, info

34	def _set_submodule(model: nn.Module, key: str, new_module: nn.Module) -> None:
35	    """Replace a nested submodule given a dotted key path (e.g. 'model.language_model')."""
36	    parts = key.split(".")
37	    parent = model
38	    for part in parts[:-1]:

43	def _generate_default_piecewise_num_tokens(max_num_tokens: int) -> List[int]:
44	    """Generate default piecewise bucket sizes when none are specified.
45	
46	    Uses powers-of-2 from 64 up to max_num_tokens. This provides ~log2(max/64)
47	    bucket sizes with at most 2x padding overhead per bucket.
48	
49	    For example, max_num_tokens=8192 → [64, 128, 256, 512, 1024, 2048, 4096, 8192]
50	    """
51	    if max_num_tokens <= 0:
52	        return []
53	
54	    buckets = []
55	    nt = 64
56	    while nt <= max_num_tokens:
57	        buckets.append(nt)
58	        nt *= 2
59	
60	    # Always include max_num_tokens as the largest bucket
61	    if not buckets or buckets[-1] != max_num_tokens:
62	        buckets.append(max_num_tokens)
63	
64	    return sorted(buckets)

67	class CompileModelConfig(TransformConfig):
68	    """Configuration for the compile model transform."""
69	
70	    cuda_graph_batch_sizes: Optional[List[int]] = Field(
71	        default=None, description="The batch sizes to use for CUDA graphs."

82	        description="The backend to use for compiling the model."
83	    )

87	    )

92	            "If null and piecewise_enabled=true, auto-generates power-of-2 buckets "
93	            "up to max_num_tokens (e.g. [64, 128, 256, ..., max_num_tokens])."

118	        mod: nn.Module,
119	        cm: CachedSequenceInterface,
120	        factory: ModelFactory,
121	        shared_config: SharedConfig,
122	    ) -> Tuple[nn.Module, TransformInfo]:
123	        cm.info.reset()
124	        spec_config = cm._spec_config
125	
126	        def _get_args_kwargs(bs: int) -> ArgsKwargs:
127	            if spec_config is not None:
128	                cm.info.set_capture_batch(batch_size=bs, max_draft_len=spec_config.max_draft_len)
129	                return (), {**cm.named_args, "cache_seq_interface": cm}
130	            cm.info.set_capture_batch(batch_size=bs)
131	            return (), cm.named_args
132	
133	        resource_input_names = list(cm.resource_names)
134	        if spec_config is not None and "cache_seq_interface" not in resource_input_names:
135	            resource_input_names.append("cache_seq_interface")
136	        extra_kwargs = {"resource_input_names": tuple(resource_input_names)}
137	        config_overrides = {}
138	        if self.config.piecewise_enabled:
139	            extra_kwargs["piecewise_seq_info"] = cm.info
140	            extra_kwargs["piecewise_named_args_fn"] = lambda: cm.named_args
141	
142	            max_seq = cm.info.max_seq_len
143	            max_batch = cm.info.max_batch_size
144	            batch_capacity = (max_batch - 1) * max_seq + 1
145	
146	            # Auto-generate piecewise_num_tokens if not explicitly specified
147	            if self.config.piecewise_num_tokens is None:
148	                max_num_tokens = cm.info.max_num_tokens
149	                auto_buckets = _generate_default_piecewise_num_tokens(max_num_tokens)
150	                config_overrides["piecewise_num_tokens"] = auto_buckets
151	                ad_logger.info(
152	                    f"Auto-generated piecewise_num_tokens from max_num_tokens={max_num_tokens}: "
153	                    f"{auto_buckets}"
154	                )
155	            else:
156	                # Filter out buckets < 3 (mixed batch needs at least 3 tokens)
157	                valid_buckets = [nt for nt in self.config.piecewise_num_tokens if nt >= 3]
158	                dropped = [nt for nt in self.config.piecewise_num_tokens if nt < 3]
159	                if dropped:
160	                    ad_logger.warning(
161	                        f"Dropping piecewise_num_tokens {dropped} (too small for mixed batch, "
162	                        f"minimum is 3). Remaining: {valid_buckets}"
163	                    )
164	                config_overrides["piecewise_num_tokens"] = valid_buckets
165	
166	            # Filter out buckets that exceed the mixed-batch capacity
167	            buckets = config_overrides.get(
168	                "piecewise_num_tokens", self.config.piecewise_num_tokens or []
169	            )
170	            over = [nt for nt in buckets if nt > batch_capacity]
171	            if over:
172	                buckets = [nt for nt in buckets if nt <= batch_capacity]
173	                ad_logger.warning(
174	                    f"Dropping piecewise buckets {over} that exceed mixed-batch capacity "
175	                    f"({max_batch - 1} seqs * {max_seq} tokens + 1 decode = {batch_capacity}). "
176	                    f"Remaining: {buckets}"
177	                )
178	                config_overrides["piecewise_num_tokens"] = buckets
179	
180	        # Merge config with any overrides
181	        config_dict = self.config.model_dump()
182	        config_dict.update(config_overrides)
183	
184	        def _compile_one(
185	            target: nn.Module,
186	            *,
187	            full_model: Optional[nn.Module] = None,
188	        ) -> nn.Module:
189	            backend_kwargs = {
190	                "get_args_kwargs_for_compile": _get_args_kwargs,
191	                **extra_kwargs,
192	                **config_dict,
193	            }
194	            if full_model is not None:
195	                backend_kwargs["full_model"] = full_model
196	            compiler_backend = CompileBackendRegistry.get(self.config.backend)(
197	                target,
198	                **backend_kwargs,
199	            )
200	            return compiler_backend.compile()
201	
202	        if self.config.piecewise_enabled:
203	            # Walk the module tree and collect the top-level GraphModules to compile.
204	            # Once a GM is found, its children are skipped (they're part of the GM).
205	            compile_targets = []
206	            seen = set()
207	            if isinstance(mod, GraphModule):
208	                compile_targets.append(("", mod))
209	                seen.add("")
210	            for name, submod in mod.named_modules():
211	                if any(p == "" or name.startswith(p + ".") for p in seen):
212	                    continue
213	                if isinstance(submod, GraphModule):
214	                    compile_targets.append((name, submod))
215	                    seen.add(name)
216	
217	            if compile_targets:
218	                ad_logger.info(
219	                    f"CompileModel: compiling {len(compile_targets)} GraphModule(s): "
220	                    f"{[name or '(root)' for name, _ in compile_targets]}"
221	                )
222	                for gm_key, gm in compile_targets:
223	                    compiled_gm = _compile_one(gm, full_model=mod if gm_key else None)
224	                    if gm_key:
225	                        _set_submodule(mod, gm_key, compiled_gm)
226	                    else:
227	                        mod = compiled_gm
228	                mod_compiled = mod
229	            else:
230	                mod_compiled = _compile_one(mod)
231	        else:
232	            mod_compiled = _compile_one(mod)
233	
234	        # store info object about the transform
235	        info = TransformInfo(skipped=False, num_matches=1, is_clean=True, has_valid_shapes=True)
236	
237	        return mod_compiled, info

94	def _round_up_to_closest(batch_sizes: List[int], bs: int) -> Optional[int]:
95	    """Return closest batch size larger or equal to bs."""
96	    if bs > max(batch_sizes, default=0):
97	        return None
98	    return min(batch_sizes, key=lambda x: (x < bs, abs(x - bs)), default=None)

101	def _generate_dummy_request(
102	    resource_manager: ResourceManager, request_id: int, **request_kwargs
103	) -> Optional[LlmRequest]:
104	    # get resource managers we want
105	    kv_cache_manager: KVCacheManager = resource_manager.get_resource_manager(
106	        ResourceManagerType.KV_CACHE_MANAGER
107	    )
108	    slot_manager: SeqSlotManager = resource_manager.get_resource_manager(
109	        ResourceManagerType.SEQ_SLOT_MANAGER
110	    )
111	
112	    # check if it's a hybrid kv-cache manager
113	    is_hybrid_cache = isinstance(kv_cache_manager, BaseMambaCacheManager)
114	
115	    # check if we have a free page and free state available
116	    if not kv_cache_manager.get_num_free_blocks():
117	        return None
118	    if is_hybrid_cache and not kv_cache_manager.mamba_cache_free_blocks:
119	        return None
120	
121	    # generate a dummy request
122	    dummy_request = kv_cache_manager.add_dummy_requests([request_id], **request_kwargs)[0]
123	    dummy_request.is_cuda_graph_dummy = True
124	
125	    # NOTE: hack to avoid blocking a slot for the dummy request
126	    dummy_request.py_seq_slot = slot_manager.get_max_resource_count()
127	    dummy_request.seq_slot = dummy_request.py_seq_slot
128	
129	    return dummy_request

132	def maybe_pad_for_cuda_graph(func):
133	    def wrapper(
134	        self: "ADEngine",
135	        scheduled_requests: ScheduledRequests,
136	        resource_manager: ResourceManager,
137	        *args,
138	        **kwargs,
139	    ):
140	        def _call_func():
141	            return func(self, scheduled_requests, resource_manager, *args, **kwargs)
142	
143	        def _call_func_eager():
144	            # Force captured-graph wrappers to short-circuit to eager (see
145	            # BypassCapturedGraphs): a rank whose shapes match a captured graph would
146	            # otherwise replay with stale capture-time per-rank scalar args.
147	            with BypassCapturedGraphs():
148	                return _call_func()
149	
150	        # Pick the cudagraph-fallback path: only attention-DP mixed mode needs the
151	        # eager bypass (stale per-rank scalar args). Without attention-DP all ranks
152	        # share shapes, so the plain eager call keeps piecewise cudagraph for prefill
153	        # — bypassing would force every prefill eager (a needless low-concurrency hit).
154	        _fallback = (
155	            _call_func_eager
156	            if (self.enable_attention_dp and self.dist_config.tp_size > 1)
157	            else _call_func
158	        )
159	
160	        # check conditions for current rank
161	        can_run_cuda_graph = self.cuda_graph_used and scheduled_requests.can_run_cuda_graph
162	        batch_size = scheduled_requests.batch_size
163	
164	        # generate a persistent dummy request right away to ensure we can reserve the necessary
165	        # resources (kv page and state) the first time we can actually run cuda graph according to
166	        # this rank
167	        if can_run_cuda_graph and self.padding_dummy_request is None:
168	            self.padding_dummy_request = _generate_dummy_request(
169	                resource_manager,
170	                request_id=CUDA_GRAPH_DUMMY_REQUEST_ID,
171	                is_gen=True,
172	                max_num_draft_tokens=self.max_total_draft_tokens,
173	                use_mrope=False,
174	                max_beam_width=self.max_beam_width,
175	            )
176	
177	        # check if we can pad the batch based on the availability of the dummy request
178	        can_pad = self.padding_dummy_request is not None
179	
180	        # in attention DP mode, we check all ranks
181	        if self.enable_attention_dp and self.dist_config.tp_size > 1:
182	            assert self.dist is not None, "Distributed object is required for attention DP mode"
183	            all_rank_info = self.dist.tp_allgather([can_run_cuda_graph, can_pad, batch_size])
184	        else:
185	            all_rank_info = [[can_run_cuda_graph, can_pad, batch_size]]
186	
187	        # now let's check if we can in principle run cuda graph across all ranks
188	        can_run_cuda_graph_all = all(r_info[0] for r_info in all_rank_info)
189	
190	        if not can_run_cuda_graph_all:
191	            return _fallback()
192	
193	        # get closest cudagraph batch size based on max_batch_size across ALL ranks
194	        # NOTE: we assume uniform cudagraph batch sizes across all ranks ensuring all ranks get the
195	        # same closest cudagraph batch size here based on the max batch size across all ranks
196	        max_batch_size = max(r_info[2] for r_info in all_rank_info)
197	        cg_batch_size = _round_up_to_closest(self.cuda_graph_batch_sizes, max_batch_size)
198	
199	        if cg_batch_size is None:
200	            return _fallback()
201	
202	        # let's check if all ranks can pad the batch if they need to
203	        can_pad_all = all(r_info[1] or (r_info[2] == cg_batch_size) for r_info in all_rank_info)
204	
205	        # fall back if we cannot run cudagraph due to padding issues
206	        if not can_pad_all:
207	            return _fallback()
208	
209	        # check actual amount of padding needed
210	        num_padding = cg_batch_size - batch_size
211	
212	        # we should only hit this point for either of these conditions
213	        assert num_padding == 0 or (num_padding > 0 and self.padding_dummy_request is not None), (
214	            "Padding should not be needed or available at this point"
215	        )
216	
217	        # no padding needed on current rank
218	        if num_padding == 0:
219	            return _call_func()
220	
221	        # pad the scheduled requests with the dummy request
222	        scheduled_requests.generation_requests.extend([self.padding_dummy_request] * num_padding)
223	
224	        ret = _call_func()
225	
226	        # truncate requests to remove the dummy requests we added
227	        scheduled_requests.generation_requests = scheduled_requests.generation_requests[
228	            :-num_padding
229	        ]
230	
231	        return ret
232	
233	    return wrapper

236	def _compute_window_local_view(
237	    all_indices: Sequence[int],
238	    front_removed: int,
239	    end_compute_i: int,
240	    group_window: int,
241	    tokens_per_block: int,
242	) -> Tuple[List[int], int, int, int]:
243	    """Compute the window-coherent metadata view for one (request, window) pair.
244	
245	    The C++ KVCacheManager allocates blocks linearly during prefill and only
246	    front-evicts during generation (kvCacheManager.cpp::adjustBlocksIfNeeded
247	    is invoked from addToken, not addSequenceBatch).  Two regimes follow:
248	
249	      * Pre-eviction (typically a single long prefill that has not yet been
250	        decoded past the window): ``front_removed == 0`` and the live page
251	        list covers the full sequence.  The kernel needs every live page and
252	        the unclamped local cache length; the sliding-window mask is applied
253	        inside the kernel.
254	
255	      * Post-eviction (decode/extend has advanced past the window): the C++
256	        side has bumped ``mNumFrontBlocksRemovedPerWindow`` without popping
257	        ``mCacheBlockIds``, so the head of the page list is stale.  After
258	        slicing those entries off, the live cache length in window-local
259	        coords is ``end_compute_i - front_removed * tokens_per_block`` —
260	        bounded above by ``group_window + tokens_per_block - 1`` by the
261	        ``while (live >= window + page_size) detachFrontBlock`` loop.
262	
263	    Both regimes collapse to a single rule: trust the C++ accounting and
264	    derive the local cache length from ``end_compute_i`` and ``front_removed``
265	    rather than artificially clamping to ``group_window``.  Disagreement
266	    between the Python and C++ sides (e.g. a caller passing a stale
267	    ``end_compute_i`` against a fresher ``front_removed``) is asserted on
268	    rather than silently masked.
269	
270	    Args:
271	        all_indices: Full historical page list from ``get_cache_indices``,
272	            including stale front entries when eviction has fired.
273	        front_removed: Count of stale front entries, from
274	            ``get_num_front_blocks_removed``.
275	        end_compute_i: Global token position after this step's tokens are
276	            processed (``input_pos + seq_len``).
277	        group_window: Sliding-window size for this pool.  Currently only used
278	            for the defensive sanity assertion below; the window mask itself
279	            is applied inside the kernel via the ``sliding_window`` constant.
280	        tokens_per_block: Cache page size.
281	
282	    Returns:
283	        active_indices: the live slice of all_indices to hand the kernel.
284	        extra_page: the next page after the live slice (used by the overlap
285	            scheduler's deferred-page insertion), or -1 when there is no
286	            slot past the live region.
287	        seq_len_with_cache: window-local cache length the kernel should see.
288	        last_page_len: derived from seq_len_with_cache and tokens_per_block.
289	    """
290	    live_len = len(all_indices) - front_removed
291	    # Window-local cache length: how many tokens the live pages actually hold.
292	    # Pre-eviction: end_compute_i (the full prefill so far).
293	    # Post-eviction: end_compute_i - front_removed * page_size (capped above by
294	    # window + page_size - 1 thanks to the C++ eviction loop).
295	    local_cache_len = end_compute_i - front_removed * tokens_per_block
296	    # Live cache length must fit inside the live pages.  The C++ KVCacheManager
297	    # keeps the two in sync (it bumps front_removed exactly as it frees blocks,
298	    # and allocates new ones for incoming tokens), so a violation means the
299	    # Python side and C++ side disagree on either end_compute_i or
300	    # front_removed -- fail loudly rather than silently clamp.
301	    live_capacity = live_len * tokens_per_block
302	    assert local_cache_len <= live_capacity, (
303	        f"window-local cache length {local_cache_len} exceeds live page capacity "
304	        f"{live_capacity} (live_len={live_len}, end_compute_i={end_compute_i}, "
305	        f"front_removed={front_removed}, tokens_per_block={tokens_per_block}). "
306	        f"C++ KVCacheManager accounting is expected to keep these in sync."
307	    )
308	    active_token_count = local_cache_len
309	    # Sanity: live cache should never exceed window + one spillover page once
310	    # front-eviction has fired (the C++ ``while (live >= window + page_size)
311	    # detachFrontBlock`` loop guarantees this).  Pre-eviction (front_removed=0,
312	    # e.g. a single long prefill) may legitimately exceed the window because
313	    # blocks are allocated linearly for the full prompt and only detached
314	    # during generation -- so we skip the check there.
315	    assert active_token_count <= group_window + tokens_per_block or front_removed == 0, (
316	        f"window-local cache length {active_token_count} exceeds "
317	        f"window {group_window} + page_size {tokens_per_block} "
318	        f"(end_compute_i={end_compute_i}, front_removed={front_removed})"
319	    )
320	    # Pages needed to address active_token_count tokens; equals live_len in
321	    # the common case (post-eviction live = window + spillover, pre-eviction
322	    # live = ceil(end_compute_i / page_size)).
323	    pages_for_active = (active_token_count + tokens_per_block - 1) // tokens_per_block
324	    num_active = min(live_len, pages_for_active)
325	    active_indices = list(all_indices[front_removed : front_removed + num_active])
326	    extra_slot_idx = front_removed + num_active
327	    extra_page = all_indices[extra_slot_idx] if len(all_indices) > extra_slot_idx else -1
328	    if active_token_count > 0:
329	        last_page_len = (active_token_count - 1) % tokens_per_block + 1
330	    else:
331	        last_page_len = 0
332	    return active_indices, extra_page, active_token_count, last_page_len
333

335	def _compute_cyclic_full_view(
336	    all_indices: Sequence[int],
337	    end_compute_i: int,
338	    tokens_per_block: int,
339	) -> Tuple[List[int], int, int, int]:
340	    """Compute the metadata view for a cyclic-SWA kernel (trtllm).
341	
342	    Unlike ``_compute_window_local_view`` (which slices the block table down to
343	    the live sliding window for kernels that cannot cyclic-index), the trtllm
344	    ``thop.attention`` kernel applies the sliding-window mask itself by wrapping
345	    KV reads modulo the attention window. It therefore needs:
346	
347	      * the FULL per-window block table (``all_indices`` verbatim, including any
348	        stale front-evicted entries -- the kernel's modulo indexing skips them),
349	        and
350	      * the GLOBAL (un-window-capped) KV length ``end_compute_i``.
351	
352	    This mirrors the PyTorch backend, which copies the manager's full block list
353	    from index 0 and passes ``host_past_key_value_lengths == total KV length``.
354	
355	    Returns the same 4-tuple shape as ``_compute_window_local_view``:
356	    ``(active_indices, extra_page, seq_len_with_cache, last_page_len)``.
357	    ``extra_page`` is always -1: the full table already contains the next page,
358	    so the overlap scheduler needs no deferred-page insertion.
359	    """
360	    active_indices = list(all_indices)
361	    seq_len_with_cache = end_compute_i
362	    if seq_len_with_cache > 0:
363	        last_page_len = (seq_len_with_cache - 1) % tokens_per_block + 1
364	    else:
365	        last_page_len = 0
366	    return active_indices, -1, seq_len_with_cache, last_page_len

369	class ADEngine(ModelEngine):
370	    """The AutoDeploy Engine (ADEngine) is the main engine interface to execute AutoDeploy models.
371	
372	    It follows the `ModelEngine` abstractions and is responsible for building the ad-optimized
373	    model, converting TRT-LLM scheduled requests into ad-native (pytorch-native) inputs, running
374	    the model, and returning correctly formatted logits.
375	    """
376	
377	    @property
378	    def _device(self) -> DeviceLikeType:
379	        return self.cache_seq_interface.device
380	
381	    @classmethod
382	    def build_from_config(
383	        cls,
384	        ad_config: LlmArgs,
385	        dist_config: Optional[DistConfig] = None,
386	        # deprecation: Mapping will soon be replaced entirely by DistConfig
387	        mapping: Optional[Mapping] = None,
388	        dist: Optional[Distributed] = None,
389	    ):
390	        """Build the ADEngine using the LlmArgs that gets passed through from the LLM."""
391	
392	        # update device to contain the current default device if it's in cuda
393	        device = torch.device(ad_config.device)
394	        if device.type == "cuda" and device.index is None:
395	            device = torch.device(f"cuda:{torch.cuda.current_device()}")
396	        device = str(device)
397	
398	        factory = ad_config.create_factory()
399	
400	        # Initialize CachedSequenceInterface - it will create SequenceInfo internally
401	        # using tokens_per_block from kv_cache_config
402	        cache_seq_interface = CachedSequenceInterface(
403	            max_seq_len=ad_config.max_seq_len,
404	            max_batch_size=ad_config.max_batch_size,
405	            device=device,
406	            kv_cache_config=ad_config.kv_cache_config,
407	            max_num_tokens=ad_config.max_num_tokens,
408	            vocab_size_padded=factory.vocab_size_padded,
409	            spec_config=ad_config.speculative_config,
410	            requires_uniform_kv_caches=ad_config.requires_uniform_kv_caches,
411	            reject_unmanaged_persistent_caches=ad_config.reject_unmanaged_persistent_caches,
412	        )
413	
414	        reporting_info = ReportingInfo(
415	            print_log=False,
416	            enable_iter_perf_stats=ad_config.enable_iter_perf_stats,
417	            enable_iter_req_stats=ad_config.enable_iter_req_stats,
418	        )
419	
420	        build_and_optimize = InferenceOptimizer(
421	            factory=factory, config=ad_config.transforms, dist_config=dist_config
422	        )
423	
424	        # construct engine
425	        return cls(
426	            build_and_optimize,
427	            cache_seq_interface,
428	            ad_config=ad_config,
429	            dist_config=dist_config,
430	            mapping=mapping,
431	            dist=dist,
432	            reporting_info=reporting_info,
433	        )
434	
435	    @torch.inference_mode()
436	    def __init__(
437	        self,
438	        get_inference_model: GetInferenceModel,
439	        cache_seq_interface: CachedSequenceInterface,
440	        ad_config: Optional[LlmArgs] = None,
441	        dist_config: Optional[DistConfig] = None,
442	        mapping: Optional[Mapping] = None,
443	        dist: Optional[Distributed] = None,
444	        reporting_info: ReportingInfo = ReportingInfo(),
445	    ) -> None:
446	        """Initialize the engine with model and CachedSequenceInterface.
447	
448	        Args:
449	            get_inference_model: Callable that builds the inference model.
450	            cache_seq_interface: The CachedSequenceInterface containing sequence and cache config.
451	            ad_config: Optional LLM configuration.
452	            dist_config: DistConfig (single source of truth for distributed config within AD).
453	            mapping: Mapping for external TRT-LLM APIs (KV cache, sampler, etc.).
454	            reporting_info: Reporting configuration for logging.
455	        """
456	        # NOTE (lucaslie): create a fake Namespace to satisfy PyExecutor requirements...
457	        # This is not correctly declared in the base ModelEngine class though...
458	        self.llm_args = SimpleNamespace()
459	        self.llm_args.print_iter_log = reporting_info.print_log
460	        self.llm_args.enable_iter_perf_stats = reporting_info.enable_iter_perf_stats
461	        self.llm_args.enable_iter_req_stats = reporting_info.enable_iter_req_stats
462	        self.llm_args.max_num_tokens = cache_seq_interface.info.max_num_tokens
463	        self.llm_args.max_seq_len = cache_seq_interface.info.max_seq_len
464	        # AutoDeploy does not support the sleep/wakeup feature.
465	        self.llm_args.sleep_config = None
466	        self.llm_args.multimodal_config = (
467	            ad_config.multimodal_config if ad_config else MultimodalConfig()
468	        )
469	        self.iter_counter = 0
470	        self.iter_states = {}
471	
472	        # NOTE (lucaslie): not a declared base member in the base class; required by PyExecutor...
473	        self.enable_attention_dp = dist_config.enable_attention_dp if dist_config else False
474	
475	        if ad_config is not None:
476	            self.llm_args.stream_interval = ad_config.stream_interval
477	            self.llm_args.attention_dp_config = ad_config.attention_dp_config
478	            self.llm_args.batch_wait_timeout_ms = ad_config.batch_wait_timeout_ms
479	            self.llm_args.batch_wait_timeout_iters = ad_config.batch_wait_timeout_iters
480	            self.llm_args.batch_wait_max_tokens_ratio = ad_config.batch_wait_max_tokens_ratio
481	            self.max_beam_width = ad_config.max_beam_width
482	            self.spec_config = ad_config.speculative_config
483	            self._disable_overlap_scheduler = ad_config.disable_overlap_scheduler
484	            cache_transceiver_config = ad_config.cache_transceiver_config
485	            self._cache_transceiver_enabled = (
486	                cache_transceiver_config is not None
487	                and cache_transceiver_config.backend is not None
488	            )
489	            self.llm_args.max_stats_len = ad_config.max_stats_len
490	            self._enable_chunked_prefill = getattr(ad_config, "enable_chunked_prefill", False)
491	        else:
492	            self.llm_args.stream_interval = 1
493	            self.llm_args.attention_dp_config = None
494	            self.llm_args.batch_wait_timeout_ms = 0
495	            self.llm_args.batch_wait_timeout_iters = 0
496	            self.llm_args.batch_wait_max_tokens_ratio = 0.0
497	            self.max_beam_width = 1
498	            self.spec_config = None
499	            self._disable_overlap_scheduler = False
500	            self._cache_transceiver_enabled = False
501	            self.llm_args.max_stats_len = 1000
502	            self._enable_chunked_prefill = False
503	
504	        # check for max total draft tokens
505	        if self.spec_config is not None:
506	            self.max_total_draft_tokens = self.spec_config.tokens_per_gen_step - 1
507	        else:
508	            self.max_total_draft_tokens = 0
509	
510	        # ADEngine skips PyTorchModelEngine.__init__, so set the spec-decode
511	        # flags that shared PyExecutor code expects on a ModelEngine.
512	        self.is_spec_decode = self.spec_config is not None
513	        self.enable_spec_decode = self.is_spec_decode
514	
515	        # For compatibility with PyTorchModelEngine utilities
516	        self.batch_size = cache_seq_interface.info.max_batch_size
517	
518	        # Store the cache sequence interface
519	        self.cache_seq_interface = cache_seq_interface
520	
521	        # build model

549	    def _release_cuda_graphs(self) -> None:
550	        def _reset_cuda_graph(graph: object) -> None:
551	            if isinstance(graph, torch.cuda.CUDAGraph):
552	                graph.reset()
553	
554	        model = getattr(self, "model", None)
555	        if model is not None:
556	            for module in model.modules():
557	                if module.__class__.__name__ == "CapturedGraph":
558	                    cudagraphs = getattr(module, "cudagraphs", None)
559	                    if isinstance(cudagraphs, dict):
560	                        for graph in list(cudagraphs.values()):

564	                    module._input_buffers = []

569	                    if isinstance(static_input_buffers, dict):

572	                if module.__class__.__name__ == "ADPiecewiseRunner":

582	    def _store_prefill_multimodal_metadata(
583	        self,
584	        ordered_requests: RequestList,
585	        input_pos: List[int],
586	        cu_seqlen: List[int],
587	        num_prefill_seqs: int,
588	        extra_args: Dict[str, List[torch.Tensor]],
589	    ) -> None:
590	        """Stage per-request multimodal layout metadata needed by the VLM wrapper.
591	
592	        The standard attention metadata captures request geometry (batch_info, cu_seqlen,
593	        seq_len_with_cache, input_pos), but not the original per-request multimodal span layout
594	        or multimodal special-token offsets needed to rebuild chunk-aware mRoPE positions.
595	
596	        This tensorization happens in the executor because it still has the scheduled request
597	        list, per-request chunk boundaries, input_pos, cu_seqlen, and access to the raw
598	        request-side multimodal fields (multimodal_positions, multimodal_lengths, and
599	        py_multimodal_data["layout_metadata"]). By the time control reaches the exported
600	        wrapper/modeling path, Python request objects are gone and the model call can only
601	        consume concrete tensor kwargs.
602	        """
603	        if num_prefill_seqs == 0:
604	            return
605	
606	        prefill_requests = ordered_requests[:num_prefill_seqs]
607	        if not any(getattr(req, "multimodal_positions", None) for req in prefill_requests):
608	            return
609	
610	        mm_item_cu_seqlen: List[int] = [0]
611	        mm_item_types_flat: List[int] = []
612	        mm_token_positions_flat: List[int] = []
613	        mm_token_lengths_flat: List[int] = []
614	        mm_special_offsets_cu_seqlen: List[int] = [0]
615	        mm_special_offsets_flat: List[int] = []
616	        flat_start_list: List[int] = []
617	        count_list: List[int] = []
618	        cumsum_total_mm = 0
619	
620	        for i, req in enumerate(prefill_requests):
621	            begin_compute = input_pos[i]
622	            end_compute = begin_compute + (cu_seqlen[i + 1] - cu_seqlen[i])
623	            mm_pos = getattr(req, "multimodal_positions", None)
624	            mm_len = getattr(req, "multimodal_lengths", None)
625	            layout_metadata = {}
626	            if req.py_multimodal_data:
627	                layout_metadata = req.py_multimodal_data.get(
628	                    "layout_metadata", req.py_multimodal_data
629	                )
630	            mm_item_types = layout_metadata.get("item_types", []) if layout_metadata else []
631	            mm_pos_list = list(mm_pos) if mm_pos is not None else []
632	            mm_len_list = list(mm_len) if mm_len is not None else []
633	            mm_item_types_list = list(mm_item_types)
634	            if len(mm_pos_list) != len(mm_len_list):
635	                raise ValueError(
636	                    "Mismatch between multimodal_positions and multimodal_lengths in "
637	                    f"request {i}: positions={len(mm_pos_list)}, lengths={len(mm_len_list)}"
638	                )
639	            if mm_item_types_list and len(mm_item_types_list) != len(mm_pos_list):
640	                raise ValueError(
641	                    "Mismatch between multimodal item_types and multimodal span arrays in "
642	                    f"request {i}: item_types={len(mm_item_types_list)}, "
643	                    f"positions={len(mm_pos_list)}, lengths={len(mm_len_list)}"
644	                )
645	            mm_item_cu_seqlen.append(mm_item_cu_seqlen[-1] + len(mm_pos_list))
646	            mm_item_types_flat.extend(mm_item_types_list)
647	            mm_token_positions_flat.extend(mm_pos_list)
648	            mm_token_lengths_flat.extend(mm_len_list)
649	
650	            mm_data = req.py_multimodal_data or {}
651	            flat_cumsum = mm_data.get("multimodal_embed_mask_cumsum")
652	            # special_token_offsets indices into the dense MM-token-list (which includes both embeds and specials).
653	            # It does not index into the prompt-position-indexed cumsum.
654	            special_offsets = list(
655	                mm_data.get("special_token_offsets")
656	                or (layout_metadata or {}).get("special_token_offsets", [])
657	            )
658	            mm_special_offsets_cu_seqlen.append(
659	                mm_special_offsets_cu_seqlen[-1] + len(special_offsets)
660	            )
661	            mm_special_offsets_flat.extend(special_offsets)
662	
663	            if not mm_pos or not mm_len:
664	                flat_start_list.append(0)
665	                count_list.append(0)
666	                continue
667	
668	            all_prompt_tokens = req.get_tokens(0)
669	            check_mm_embed_cumsum_if_needed(
670	                req.py_multimodal_data,
671	                begin_compute=begin_compute,
672	                end_compute=end_compute,
673	                prompt_len=len(all_prompt_tokens),
674	            )
675	            if flat_cumsum is None:
676	                # Leave flat_start / count at 0 so concatenated cursors don't advance.
677	                flat_start_list.append(0)
678	                count_list.append(0)
679	                continue
680	
681	            assert flat_cumsum.numel() == len(all_prompt_tokens), (
682	                f"embed_mask_cumsum length {flat_cumsum.numel()} != prompt length "
683	                f"{len(all_prompt_tokens)} for request {i}"
684	            )
685	            runtime = MultimodalRuntimeData(
686	                past_seen_token_num=begin_compute,
687	                chunk_end_pos=end_compute,
688	                embed_mask_cumsum=flat_cumsum,
689	            )
690	            flat_start_list.append(cumsum_total_mm + runtime.num_cached_mm_tokens)
691	            count_list.append(runtime.num_mm_tokens_in_chunk)
692	            cumsum_total_mm += runtime.total_embeds_in_request
693	
694	        extra_args["mm_item_cu_seqlen"] = [
695	            torch.tensor(mm_item_cu_seqlen, dtype=torch.int32, device="cpu")
696	        ]
697	        extra_args["mm_item_types"] = [
698	            torch.tensor(mm_item_types_flat, dtype=torch.int32, device="cpu")
699	        ]
700	        extra_args["mm_token_positions"] = [
701	            torch.tensor(mm_token_positions_flat, dtype=torch.int32, device="cpu")
702	        ]
703	        extra_args["mm_token_lengths"] = [
704	            torch.tensor(mm_token_lengths_flat, dtype=torch.int32, device="cpu")
705	        ]
706	        extra_args["mm_special_offsets_cu_seqlen"] = [
707	            torch.tensor(mm_special_offsets_cu_seqlen, dtype=torch.int32, device="cpu")
708	        ]
709	        extra_args["mm_special_offsets"] = [
710	            torch.tensor(mm_special_offsets_flat, dtype=torch.int32, device="cpu")
711	        ]
712	        # Export multimodal slice bounds whenever the current prefill step only needs a
713	        # subset of the request's multimodal embeddings. This is required for regular
714	        # chunked prefill, but also for KV-cache reuse where begin_compute > 0 even when
715	        # chunked prefill is disabled in the config.
716	        needs_mm_chunk_bounds = self._enable_chunked_prefill or any(
717	            int(input_pos[i]) > 0 and getattr(req, "multimodal_positions", None)
718	            for i, req in enumerate(prefill_requests)
719	        )
720	        if needs_mm_chunk_bounds:
721	            extra_args["mm_chunk_flat_start"] = [
722	                torch.tensor(flat_start_list, dtype=torch.int64, device="cpu")
723	            ]
724	            extra_args["mm_chunk_count"] = [
725	                torch.tensor(count_list, dtype=torch.int64, device="cpu")
726	            ]
